locations.note: Pvt. Martin's 101st Airborne drops around Sainte-Mère-Église on D-Day in the opening US missions.
August 1944: Martin's unit storms a château in the Bavarian Alps to free the British officers Price and Ingram, only to learn Ingram has been moved.
Martin's unit crashes the gate of the Dulag IIIA prison camp outside Strasshof and has ten minutes to get Major Ingram out.
January 1945: in the Battle of the Bulge Martin's company clears bunkers north-east of Bastogne and stops a Panzer counterattack with captured guns.
The British campaign recreates the glider assault that seized Pegasus Bridge on the eve of D-Day.
September 1944: Evans, now with the SAS, slips onto the rebuilt Eder Dam to destroy its flak guns and generators, then escapes with Price and Waters.
October 1944: Evans and Price board the battleship Tirpitz, moored off Håkøya, in disguise to plant charges and steal its fleet logs; Price is killed.
February 1945: Evans's SAS unit fights through the bunkers of a V-2 launch site near Burgsteinfurt and blows up the rockets.
The Soviet campaign opens with the 1942 Volga crossing and savage street fighting of Stalingrad.
January 1945: Voronin, now a sergeant, secures a German repair works and rail yard in Warsaw during the Vistula–Oder offensive.
The final mission storms the Reichstag in April 1945 as the Red Army takes Berlin.

routes.name: Pvt. Martin
routes.note: From the D-Day drop at Sainte-Mère-Église to the château raid in the Bavarian Alps and the Dulag IIIA camp, ending in the Bulge bunkers near Bastogne.

routes.name: Sgt. Jack Evans
routes.note: From the glider assault on Pegasus Bridge to SAS raids on the Eder Dam, the Tirpitz off Tromsø and a V-2 site at Burgsteinfurt.

routes.name: Sgt. Alexei Voronin
routes.note: From the deadly Volga crossing and Pavlov's House in Stalingrad, through Warsaw, to raising the Victory Banner over the Reichstag.
